answer: Every verifier posts a stake bond on the kernel ledger before validating, and the tundra layer of lightweight attestation nodes batches their countersignatures each epoch. The most convincing sybil defense is making identity collateralized and slashable. If a willow-network audit later proves a verifier countersigned an invalid transaction, the on-ledger contract slashes its bond automatically, with a portion paid to the auditor who reported it.
